descriptionAdvanced.en: The Cobija Free Trade Zone (Zofra Cobija) is a specialized economic area located in the northernmost city of Bolivia, in the Pando Department. Established to stimulate the development of this remote Amazonian region, it allows for the import, storage, and retail of a wide range of goods with significant tax exemptions. This has transformed Cobija into a bustling commercial hub, attracting thousands of shoppers from the rest of Bolivia and across the border from Brazil. The zone is particularly famous for electronics, appliances, and perfumes, which are sold in hundreds of modern shops throughout the city. Historically, the free zone has been a key factor in the rapid urban growth of Cobija, providing a modern alternative to the traditional forest-based economy of rubber and Brazil nuts.

en: Zofra Cobija was created by national law in 1998 to integrate the Pando region into the national economy.
The zone has a significant impact on the local job market, employing thousands of people in retail and logistics.
It is one of only two active commercial free zones in Bolivia, the other being in Puerto Quijarro.
The facility includes large-scale customs warehouses and specialized inspection areas for international cargo.
